name: Sliding window
whenToUse: The standard answer. One pass, no extra memory. Brute force also passes for n ≤ 100, but it checks the same elements again for every start.

card.signals: "subarray" (contiguous), rules every element of it must keep (even start, alternating parity, ≤ threshold) and "longest". Each rule only looks at one element or at two neighbours.
card.pattern: a variable-size window that restarts instead of shrinking. When a rule breaks at right, no valid window can contain both sides of the break, so left jumps straight to right (even value) or right + 1 (odd value or too big). Each index is visited once: O(n).
card.coreIdea: for each right, decide one of three things: nums[right] is too big (no window), it alternates with nums[right - 1] (the window grows), or the window cannot grow (restart at right if nums[right] is even, else no window). If a window exists, compare its length with longest.

invariant: After each round, the window nums[left..right] (when left ≤ right) starts with an even value, alternates even / odd, has no value above threshold, and is the longest such window that ends at right.
